title:
Your AI in GxP work
does not need a committee.
It needs one person
who can say *not yet*.
sub: Most mid-size companies have not named that person.

title:
Not a steering group.
Not the reviewer at
the release gate.
text:
One named person who sits with the teams while the thing is being built, understands what it actually does, and has the standing to pause it.

QA lead, CSV lead, IT compliance head, or an advisor brought in for it. The title matters less than the seat.
tag: If nobody has the seat, nobody has the job

title:
Watch what happens
when nobody can.
text:
Either everything gets a blanket no, and good low-risk work sits idle for a quarter.

Or everything gets a quiet yes, and a year later nobody can show who decided what.

title:
"Not yet" is not
a veto.
text:
A veto ends the conversation. *Not yet* is a decision with a date and a condition attached: what has to be true before this proceeds, and who confirms it.

Teams can work with that. They cannot work with silence.
tag: It is the fastest no in the building

title:
Five things that have
to be true first:
items: *A mandate* - someone senior agreed this role decides
*An early seat* - in the sprint review, not the release gate
*A written basis* - risk, not opinion, so it survives being challenged
*An escalation path* - disagreement goes somewhere, not nowhere
*Willingness to be unpopular* on a Friday afternoon

title:
Both failure modes
cost more.
text:
A blanket no means paid engineering time waiting on a governance answer that never arrives.

A quiet yes means reconstructing decisions under inspection pressure, a year later, with the people who made them gone.
tag: One is slow. The other is expensive

title:
The scarce skill is not
knowing the regulation.
text:
It is sitting with engineers all week, understanding what they are actually building, and still being able to say not yet on Friday - with a reason they accept.

That combination is rare, and it is what AI in GxP needs right now.

title:
Who says it
at your company?
text:
If the answer is nobody, that is the gap, not the framework.

Forward this to your QA, CSV or IT lead.

*Sreejith Kanhirangadan*
20 yrs CSV - big, mid and startup pharma - 10,000+ trained
